## Phạm vi
`[IoT][BatteryService][Offline Queue]` — luồng ESP32 lưu cục bộ rồi flush HTTPS sau khi mất mạng.

## Lỗi
Firmware tạo JSON batch một lần với `deviceTimestamp` tại thời điểm đo (`iot/firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:278-307`), lưu nguyên payload và idempotency key vào queue, rồi gửi lại nguyên body khi flush (`main.cpp:323-355`). BatteryService so sánh timestamp đo với `DateTime.UtcNow` và trả HTTP 400 nếu lệch quá 5 phút (`BatchIngestSensorReadingsCommandHandler.cs:101-133`). Firmware phân loại mọi 4xx là permanent failure và xóa batch khỏi queue.

Do đó chỉ cần mất kết nối hơn 5 phút là các reading hợp lệ đã lưu offline chắc chắn bị backend từ chối, sau đó bị firmware xóa vĩnh viễn. Điều này trái với `overall.md:9824-9840`, yêu cầu giữ queue đến khi backend trả 2xx và flush lại với idempotency key cũ.

## Mức độ
**P1** — deterministic telemetry data loss trên đúng resilience path dành cho outage dài.

## Cách tái hiện
1. Cho device thu thập batch hợp lệ khi backend/network unavailable để batch vào local queue.
2. Chờ hơn 5 phút.
3. Khôi phục mạng và gọi `tryFlushQueue()`.
4. Quan sát BatteryService trả 400 `clock_drift`.
5. Quan sát firmware gọi `queueDelete(epoch)` và batch không còn khả năng retry.

## Kỳ vọng / tiêu chí chấp nhận
- Phân biệt event/measurement time với thời điểm nhận; offline reading hợp lệ không bị coi là clock drift chỉ vì được flush muộn.
- Không xóa queued batch cho đến khi có phản hồi 2xx/dedup thành công, hoặc có chính sách quarantine/DLQ có thể phục hồi.
- Giữ nguyên measurement timestamp và idempotency semantics; không sửa timestamp cũ thành thời gian hiện tại để lách validation.
- Có integration test outage >5 phút: enqueue → delayed flush → persisted đúng một lần.
- Có test cho retry, replay, mixed fresh/stale batch và permanent schema/mapping error.

## Dedupe
Đã rà toàn bộ milestone `E2E` đến #996; chưa có issue mô tả xung đột giữa offline retention và clock-skew validation này.
title: [IoT][BatteryService][Offline Queue] Batches queued over five minutes are rejected as clock drift and permanently deleted

Kết quả là asset sang Customer B trong khi ticket đang xử lý vẫn thuộc Customer A, làm ownership, authorization, notification và SLA context mâu thuẫn giữa hai service.

## Bằng chứng đặc tả/source

- `overall.md:8239-8240`:
  - alert mở được giữ lại/notify hai owner;
  - ticket mở phải **block transfer**, yêu cầu đóng ticket trước.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/CQRS/Handler/BatteryAsset/TransferBatteryAssetOwnerCommandHandler.cs:24-63`: chỉ load asset, reject same owner và validate customer mới active.
- Dòng `65-83`: đổi `CustomerId`, clear `SiteId`, ghi outbox rồi commit ngay.
- Không có Ticket query/read model/guard/authorization reservation trước mutation.

## Cách tái hiện E2E

1. Customer A sở hữu BatteryAsset X.
2. Tạo ticket cho X ở trạng thái Open/Assigned/InProgress/PendingCustomer/Resolved nhưng chưa Closed theo định nghĩa “open”.
3. Admin gọi transfer-owner chuyển X sang Customer B.
4. Quan sát API trả `200`; BatteryService lưu B là owner và clear site.
5. Quan sát TicketService vẫn có ticket active gắn Customer A/asset X.

## Kết quả thực tế

Transfer thành công trong trạng thái EC-06 cấm. Hai bounded context giữ owner khác nhau cho cùng workflow đang mở.

## Kết quả mong đợi

Transfer phải trả conflict/domain error và không thay đổi asset/outbox khi bất kỳ ticket non-terminal nào còn tồn tại. Sau khi toàn bộ ticket được đóng, transfer mới được phép.

## Mức độ ảnh hưởng

**P1 — core ownership lifecycle.** Mâu thuẫn owner trên ticket đang xử lý có thể làm lộ hoặc mất quyền truy cập, gửi notification sai người và phá luồng maintenance/SLA.

- Xác định một authoritative open-ticket check từ TicketService (query API/gRPC hoặc read model được đồng bộ đáng tin cậy).
- Dùng workflow chống TOCTOU: reservation/lock hoặc saga/version contract để ticket mới không mở xen giữa check và transfer commit.
- Trả `409`/domain error chứa hướng dẫn close ticket; không emit transfer event khi bị block.
- Định nghĩa rõ terminal statuses và behavior khi TicketService unavailable (fail closed cho transfer).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mỗi trạng thái ticket non-terminal đều block transfer.
- [ ] Closed/Cancelled terminal theo business rule cho phép transfer.
- [ ] TicketService timeout/unavailable không cho transfer im lặng.
- [ ] Concurrent ticket-create và transfer không thể cùng commit thành trạng thái vi phạm.
- [ ] Khi block: owner/site/outbox/audit không thay đổi.
- [ ] E2E test xuyên BatteryService↔TicketService cover open/closed/race/retry.

## Test hiện tại / khoảng trống

- Battery transfer handler/validation targeted: **7/7 pass**.
- Bốn handler test hiện tại chỉ cover missing asset, same owner, inactive customer và happy path; không dựng open-ticket composition.

## Dedupe

- #821 là lifecycle events thiếu consumer/notification/reroute downstream.
- Lỗi này là synchronous precondition EC-06 phải ngăn commit; thêm consumer sau commit không thể sửa một transfer vốn phải bị từ chối.

## Tóm tắt lỗi

Firmware lưu deadline dưới dạng `uint32_t millis() + delay` nhưng kiểm tra bằng phép so sánh tuyệt đối `millis() < deadline`. Phép so sánh này không an toàn khi bộ đếm `millis()` rollover sau khoảng 49,7 ngày.

Tùy thời điểm failure và thời điểm thiết bị online lại, firmware có thể:

- bỏ qua backoff và retry liên tục trước rollover; hoặc
- coi một deadline đã qua là còn ở tương lai và không flush queue/provision lại gần một chu kỳ `uint32_t` đầy (tối đa khoảng 49,7 ngày).

## Bằng chứng source

- `iot/firmware-esp32/src/net/backoff.cpp:62`: `_nextRetryMs = platformMillis() + finalDelay;` có wrap tự nhiên trên `uint32_t`.
- `iot/firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:321`: `if (millis() < s_backoff.nextRetryAt()) return;` so sánh tuyệt đối, không rollover-safe.
- `iot/firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:106-120`: provisioning retry dùng cùng pattern `s_nextAttemptMs = millis() + 30000` và `millis() < s_nextAttemptMs`.
- `iot/firmware-esp32/src/net/backoff.h:52-54`: API/comment còn hướng caller dùng phép so sánh không an toàn này.

Các scheduler khác đã dùng subtraction/signed-delta đúng hơn (`millis() - lastData`, `static_cast<int32_t>(millis() - deadline)`), nên lỗi nằm cụ thể ở hai call site trên.

## Reproduction số học xác định

### Retry storm trước rollover

1. Giả lập `now = 0xFFFFFF00` (`4,294,967,040 ms`).
2. Backoff `300,000 ms` tạo wrapped deadline `299,744`.
3. Check hiện tại: `4,294,967,040 < 299,744` là `false`.
4. Firmware retry ngay thay vì chờ 5 phút, rồi có thể lặp ở mỗi loop trong phần thời gian trước rollover.

Rollover-safe signed delta cho cùng input là `int32_t(now - deadline) = -300,000`, nghĩa là phải tiếp tục chờ.

### Queue bị stall sau rollover

1. Có deadline cũ `0xFFFFFF00` nhưng thiết bị offline/không chạy flush tại thời điểm deadline.
2. Sau rollover, thiết bị online ở `now = 0x00000100`.
3. Check hiện tại: `256 < 4,294,967,040` là `true`, nên return dù deadline đã qua 512 ms.
4. Condition chỉ hết khi `millis()` lại tiến gần deadline cũ, có thể mất gần 49,7 ngày.

Signed delta đúng là `int32_t(now - deadline) = 512`, nghĩa là deadline đã qua và phải retry ngay.

## Kết quả thực tế

- Backoff/provision cadence sai qua rollover.
- Có thể tạo burst request vào backend/broker recovery path.
- Offline telemetry queue có thể không được flush trong thời gian rất dài dù Wi-Fi/NTP đã healthy.

## Kết quả mong đợi

Mọi scheduler dựa trên `millis()` phải hoạt động đúng xuyên rollover, với delay nhỏ hơn nửa range `uint32_t`, không retry sớm và không stall sau deadline.

## Mức độ ảnh hưởng

**P2.** Thiết bị production có thể chạy liên tục quá 49,7 ngày. Lỗi làm mất độ tin cậy của offline telemetry/recovery và có thể tạo tải retry lớn; không cần input độc hại.

## Hướng sửa đề xuất

- Cung cấp helper duy nhất, ví dụ `timeReached(now, deadline) => static_cast<int32_t>(now - deadline) >= 0`.
- Không expose deadline rồi yêu cầu caller tự so sánh; thêm `Backoff::isReady(now)` hoặc lưu delay/elapsed time.
- Áp dụng helper cho cả `tryFlushQueue` và `ensureProvisioned`.
- Audit tất cả scheduler `millis()` còn lại và giữ delay dưới `INT32_MAX`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit test deadline trước rollover + delay qua rollover không retry sớm.
- [ ] Unit test deadline trước rollover và `now` sau rollover retry đúng ngay khi đã tới hạn.
- [ ] Queue flush không stall khi reconnect sau rollover.
- [ ] Provision retry giữ đúng 30 giây qua rollover.
- [ ] Backoff 2 giây–5 phút giữ đúng tolerance/jitter qua rollover.
- [ ] Không còn raw absolute comparison `millis() < deadline`/`millis() >= deadline` trong firmware scheduler.

## Test hiện tại / khoảng trống

- Round 16: **118/118 native tests pass**, cả ba firmware environment build pass.
- `test_backoff.cpp` chỉ kiểm delay growth/cap/reset/jitter và HTTP classification; không inject clock gần `UINT32_MAX` và không test caller deadline comparison.

## Dedupe

- #914 xử lý live batch bỏ qua backoff và deterministic jitter; không xử lý rollover của deadline.
- #911 là pagination integer overflow ở backend, không liên quan firmware scheduler.
title: [IoT][Scheduler][Millis Rollover] Unsigned deadline comparisons cause retry storms or stall queue flushing for 49.7 days

## Phạm vi

`[AuthService][Delete/Reactivate][2FA]` — composition giữa self-delete, account reactivation và trusted-device login.

## Tóm tắt lỗi

Self-delete chỉ revoke refresh token và soft-delete account, nhưng giữ nguyên `TwoFactorEnabled`, 2FA secret và các `TrustedDevice`. Reactivation khôi phục account về `Active` mà không revoke/reset trust. Vì vậy, thiết bị đã được tin cậy trước khi xóa có thể đăng nhập lại sau restore và được cấp JWT trực tiếp, bỏ qua challenge 2FA.

## Bằng chứng trong source

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Account/DeleteMeCommandHandler.cs:42-56`
  - Chỉ revoke active refresh tokens rồi soft-delete account.
  - Không revoke/soft-delete `TrustedDevices`; không reset trạng thái 2FA.
- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Auth/ReactivateVerifyCommandHandler.cs:53-62`
  - Restore account và auth counters nhưng không revoke trusted devices.
- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Auth/LoginCommandHandler.cs:198-232,347-366`
  - Trusted-device row còn active, cùng fingerprint và IP prefix sẽ skip challenge 2FA và gọi `IssueAsync` cấp token.

## Cách tái hiện E2E

1. Bật 2FA cho account.
2. Login bằng TOTP/SMS với `TrustDevice=true` để tạo trusted-device row (TTL mặc định 30 ngày).
3. Gọi `DELETE /api/accounts/me` trên account đó.
4. Trong cửa sổ reactivation, request OTP và hoàn tất restore account.
5. Login lại từ cùng device fingerprint/user-agent và cùng IP prefix.
6. Quan sát response trả access/refresh token trực tiếp với message trusted-device, không yêu cầu TOTP/SMS.

## Kết quả thực tế

Trusted device từ lifecycle cũ sống qua self-delete/reactivation và tiếp tục là bằng chứng second factor hợp lệ.

## Kết quả mong đợi

Self-delete hoặc reactivation phải tạo security epoch mới: mọi trusted device cũ bị revoke. Lần login đầu tiên sau restore phải thực hiện đầy đủ 2FA trước khi người dùng có thể trust device lại.

## Mức độ ảnh hưởng

**P2.** Cần có trusted device cũ, cùng fingerprint/IP và OTP reactivation hợp lệ, nhưng đây vẫn là stale security credential làm bypass 2FA ngay sau một account lifecycle reset.

## Hướng sửa đề xuất

- Revoke tất cả trusted devices trong cùng transaction self-delete; hoặc bắt buộc revoke trong transaction reactivation trước khi account active.
- Cân nhắc reset/rotate 2FA secret và backup codes theo policy reactivation; tối thiểu phải clear trust.
- Dùng security epoch/version trên account và trusted device để mọi credential/trust từ epoch cũ tự vô hiệu.
- Audit rõ số trusted devices bị revoke và lý do `self_delete`/`reactivation`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sau self-delete, không còn trusted device active cho account.
- [ ] Reactivation không phục hồi trust từ lifecycle trước.
- [ ] Login đầu tiên sau restore với cùng fingerprint/IP vẫn trả 2FA challenge.
- [ ] Sau khi verify 2FA lại, user có thể tạo trusted device mới bình thường.
- [ ] Có integration test xuyên suốt trust → delete → reactivate → login.
- [ ] Retry delete/reactivate không tạo partial security state.

## Test đã chạy / khoảng trống

- Targeted DeleteMe/reactivation/auth tests nằm trong batch **40/40 pass**.
- DeleteMe tests hiện chỉ xác nhận soft-delete và refresh-token revoke; chưa cover composition với reactivation/trusted login.

## Dedupe

- #945 xử lý profile tombstone sau reactivation, không liên quan trusted-device/2FA.
- #925 xử lý access-token revocation ở downstream service, không xử lý stale trusted device.
- #396 là feature trusted-device gốc, không phải defect lifecycle này.
title: [AuthService][Delete/Reactivate][2FA] Trusted devices survive self-delete and bypass 2FA after account restoration

## Phạm vi

`[AuthService][2FA][Replay]` — `POST /api/auth/login/verify-2fa` và Redis challenge store.

## Tóm tắt lỗi

2FA challenge không được claim/consume atomically. Handler đọc challenge, tăng attempts, verify code, tạo token/session và commit DB; chỉ sau đó mới xóa Redis challenge. Nhiều request song song dùng cùng challenge và cùng code hợp lệ có thể đều đọc challenge trước lần xóa đầu tiên và mỗi request đều tạo một session.

## Bằng chứng trong source

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Infrastructure/Implements/Services/TwoFactorChallengeStore.cs:47-72`: `GetAsync` chỉ đọc challenge, không claim/consume.
- Dòng `75-80`: `IncrementAttemptsAsync` chỉ dùng Redis `HINCRBY`; các giá trị 1..5 đều được handler chấp nhận.
- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Auth/Verify2FALoginCommandHandler.cs:70-75`: Get và increment là hai operation riêng.
- Dòng `198-241`: `IssueAsync`, side effects và `SaveChangesAsync` xảy ra trước invalidation.
- Dòng `242`: challenge mới bị `InvalidateAsync`/`KeyDelete`.

Comment tại `Verify2FALoginCommandHandler.cs:331-341` có thừa nhận race nhưng kết luận request thứ hai không thể tạo session sau invalidation. Kết luận này không đúng với ordering: request thứ hai đã giữ challenge trong local state và không re-check Redis trước `IssueAsync`.

## Cách tái hiện E2E

1. Login account có 2FA để nhận một challenge token.
2. Chuẩn bị một TOTP đang hợp lệ (cũng cần kiểm tra SMS OTP và backup code).
3. Dùng barrier gửi đồng thời 2–5 request `verify-2fa` với cùng challenge và code.
4. Giữ cả request đi qua `GetAsync` trước khi cho tiếp tục.
5. Quan sát nhiều response `200` chứa các access/refresh token khác nhau.
6. Kiểm tra DB có nhiều refresh-token/session row từ một challenge.

## Kết quả thực tế

Một challenge one-time có thể sinh nhiều session. Xóa key ở request đầu không hủy local state của các request còn lại. Concurrent-session policy không đảm bảo ngăn lỗi: giới hạn mặc định cho phép nhiều session và các request song song có thể cùng quan sát persisted count cũ.

## Kết quả mong đợi

Mỗi challenge chỉ được đúng một request claim thành công. Mọi request concurrent/replay khác phải trả lỗi xác định và tuyệt đối không tạo JWT, refresh token, audit success hoặc trusted device.

## Mức độ ảnh hưởng

**P1 — authentication replay.** Second-factor challenge được thiết kế one-time nhưng có thể replay đồng thời để nhân bản credential/session, làm suy yếu session control và khả năng thu hồi theo phiên.

## Hướng sửa đề xuất

- Thêm atomic `TryClaimAsync` bằng Redis Lua/transaction: kiểm tra tồn tại, attempts/claimed state và chuyển sang claimed trong một operation.
- Claim phải diễn ra trước mọi token/session side effect.
- Định nghĩa state machine `pending → claimed → completed`; nếu downstream fail, dùng idempotency/reconciliation có giới hạn thay vì mở lại challenge mù quáng.
- Invalidation SMS OTP/backup code cũng phải tương thích với exactly-once challenge consumption.
- Không dựa vào session-limit handler để chữa replay.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 2–20 request song song cùng challenge/code chỉ có đúng 1 success.
- [ ] Chỉ tạo đúng 1 refresh-token/session row và 1 chuỗi audit success.
- [ ] Các request thua trả cùng error contract (`409`/`422`) và không có side effect.
- [ ] Áp dụng cho TOTP, SMS OTP và backup code.
- [ ] Restart/timeout giữa claim và commit có cơ chế idempotent/reconciliation được test.
- [ ] Redis Lua/transaction tests cover TTL, missing key, max attempts và concurrent claim.
- [ ] Sửa/xóa comment hiện tại mô tả sai guarantee.

## Test đã chạy / khoảng trống

- Batch AuthService mục tiêu: **40/40 pass**.
- Trong đó handler Verify2FA và flow integration hiện chỉ chạy tuần tự; không có barrier/concurrent replay assertion.

## Dedupe

- #865 là limiter partition bỏ qua challenge token, không phải atomic consumption.
- #889 là concurrent session-cap policy, không bảo đảm one-time challenge.
- #926 là SMS outbox commit, không liên quan replay.
title: [AuthService][2FA][Replay] Challenge consumption is non-atomic, allowing concurrent verification requests to mint multiple sessions

## Phạm vi

`[AuthService]` — các flow thay đổi thông tin bảo mật và thu hồi quyền truy cập:

- `PATCH /api/accounts/me/password`
- `POST /api/accounts/me/2fa/disable`
- `POST /api/admin/accounts/{id}/merge`

## Tóm tắt lỗi

Ba flow trên commit trạng thái chính trong PostgreSQL trước, rồi mới thực hiện các bước thu hồi bảo mật ở Redis hoặc thu hồi trusted device. Nếu bước hậu-commit lỗi, API trả `500` dù mutation chính đã thành công. Lần retry không thể hoàn tất phần còn thiếu vì precondition đã thay đổi hoặc account nguồn đã bị tombstone.

Kết quả là access token hoặc trusted device đáng lẽ phải bị thu hồi vẫn còn hiệu lực, và hệ thống không có durable reconciliation để tự sửa.

## Bằng chứng trong source

### ChangePassword

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Account/ChangePasswordCommandHandler.cs:100-126`: đổi password, revoke refresh token và `SaveChangesAsync`.
- Dòng `145`: ghi Redis account cutoff sau commit.
- Dòng `149`: revoke trusted devices sau cutoff.

Nếu Redis/Mediator lỗi sau dòng 126, password đã đổi nhưng API trả lỗi. Retry bằng mật khẩu cũ không vượt qua validation, nên cutoff/trusted-device revocation không được reconcile.

### Disable2FA

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Auth/Disable2FACommandHandler.cs:91-111`: tắt 2FA, xóa secret/backup code và commit.
- Dòng `115`: revoke trusted devices sau commit.
- Dòng `48-56`: retry khi 2FA đã tắt trả success sớm, không chạy lại revocation.

### MergeAccount

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Application/CQRS/Handler/Admin/MergeAccountCommandHandler.cs:82-195`: tombstone secondary account, revoke refresh token và commit.
- Dòng `198`: Redis cutoff chỉ được ghi sau commit.
- Dòng `55-60`: retry không tìm thấy secondary account do đã bị xóa mềm.

## Cách tái hiện

1. Đăng nhập và giữ một access token/refresh session đang hoạt động; với flow 2FA, tạo thêm một trusted device.
2. Fault-inject Redis hoặc handler revoke trusted device để nó throw ngay sau `SaveChangesAsync`.
3. Gọi một trong ba endpoint nêu trên.
4. Quan sát API trả `500`, nhưng PostgreSQL đã chứa password mới / trạng thái 2FA disabled / secondary account đã tombstone.
5. Retry cùng request.
6. Quan sát retry không thể chạy lại bước revoke còn thiếu.
7. Kiểm tra cutoff/trusted-device state: trạng thái bảo mật cũ vẫn còn active.

## Kết quả thực tế

- Mutation chính đã commit nhưng response báo lỗi.
- Revocation hậu-commit bị mất vĩnh viễn nếu không có thao tác thủ công.
- Retry không idempotent và không tự chữa partial success.

## Kết quả mong đợi

Mutation chính và ý định revocation phải tạo thành một workflow bền vững: hoặc tất cả hiệu lực, hoặc phần external còn thiếu được ghi nhận và retry cho tới khi hoàn tất. Retry client phải an toàn và idempotent.

## Mức độ ảnh hưởng

**P1 — security consistency.** Password change, disable 2FA và account merge đều là security boundary. Access/trusted-device state cũ còn sống sau khi API đã thay đổi credential/account lifecycle làm suy yếu kỳ vọng thu hồi ngay lập tức.

## Hướng sửa đề xuất

- Đưa trusted-device mutation (cùng PostgreSQL) vào transaction/UoW chính trước commit.
- Ghi durable security-reconciliation/outbox record cùng transaction cho Redis cutoff và các side effect ngoài DB.
- Worker retry idempotent tới khi hoàn tất; expose trạng thái/metric/DLQ để vận hành nhận biết.
- Thiết kế retry endpoint theo operation/idempotency key hoặc cho phép reconcile khi state chính đã ở trạng thái đích.
- Không chỉ reorder external call trước commit: cách đó chuyển lỗi thành split-brain chiều ngược lại khi DB commit thất bại.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fault sau DB commit không làm mất ý định cutoff/revocation.
- [ ] Retry sau partial success hoàn tất được mọi revocation còn thiếu.
- [ ] ChangePassword không để trusted device hoặc access cutoff ở trạng thái cũ.
- [ ] Disable2FA luôn revoke toàn bộ trusted device, kể cả retry sau partial success.
- [ ] MergeAccount luôn ghi cutoff cho secondary account, kể cả Redis tạm thời unavailable.
- [ ] Có metric/log/DLQ và test worker retry/restart.
- [ ] Có fault-injection integration tests tại từng ranh giới trước/sau commit.

## Test đã chạy / khoảng trống

- Targeted `ChangePasswordCommandHandlerTests|Disable2FACommandHandlerTests`: **13/13 pass**.
- Các test hiện tại chỉ cover happy path/concurrency cơ bản, chưa fault-inject lỗi external sau commit.
- MergeAccount chưa có handler test tương ứng cho partial commit.

## Dedupe

- Khác #925: #925 là resource service không enforce revocation; lỗi này xảy ra ngay cả khi enforcement đã đúng vì cutoff chưa từng được ghi.
- Khác #898: #898 consume reset token trước DB commit; lỗi này là revocation bị mất sau DB commit.
title: [AuthService][Security Reconciliation] Post-commit revocation failures leave access/trusted-device state active and retries cannot repair

## Component

`[AuthService][Account Reactivation][AccountProfile][StaffProfile]`

## Severity

P2 High — successful account reactivation leaves hidden one-to-one profile tombstones that make profile APIs fail with unique-index 500 errors.

## Source evidence

- `DeleteAccountCommandHandler.cs:70-97` anonymizes and soft-deletes `AccountProfile` and `StaffProfile`, while retaining the account identity for the 90-day reactivation path.
- `ReactivateVerifyCommandHandler.cs` restores only the `Account`; it does not restore, remove, or otherwise reconcile either profile row.
- `AccountProfileConfiguration.cs:66,75` and `StaffProfileConfiguration.cs:62,80` use unconditional unique `AccountId` indexes plus global filters hiding soft-deleted rows.
- `UpdateMyProfile` (`:30-79`), `UpdateStaffProfile` (`:47-60`), and `AddStaffSkill` (`:31-43`) query only active profiles and create a new row when none is visible.
- The hidden tombstone still owns the same unique `AccountId`, so the insert fails with PostgreSQL `23505`.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Create an account with an AccountProfile; for Staff, also create StaffProfile.
2. Admin-delete the account, which soft-deletes/anonymizes the profile rows.
3. Reactivate the account within 90 days using a valid OTP and an email that has not been reclaimed. Reactivation returns 200.
4. Call `UpdateMyProfile`; for Staff, also try admin staff-profile update or add-skill.
5. Each handler sees no active profile and attempts a new row with the restored AccountId.
6. The unconditional one-to-one unique index rejects it; the operation returns 500.

## Actual

Account status is restored but its dependent aggregate remains in a hidden, uniqueness-blocking deleted state.

## Expected

Reactivation must atomically reconcile every restorable dependent row, or profile commands must intentionally restore/reuse the tombstone before inserting.

## Impact

- Reactivated customers cannot maintain their profile.
- Reactivated staff cannot restore operational profile/skill data and may be unusable for assignment workflows.
- The API reports successful account recovery even though core post-login features are broken.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define which anonymized profile fields can/should be restored and which must be re-entered.
- Reconcile AccountProfile and StaffProfile atomically during reactivation, or restore tombstones on first profile mutation.
- Never insert a duplicate one-to-one row while a deleted row owns the AccountId.
- Map unavoidable concurrency conflicts to a controlled response.
- Add end-to-end admin-delete→reactivate→customer-profile and staff-profile/skill tests.
- Verify audit, privacy/anonymization, and role-specific profile invariants after restore.

## Dedupe

Distinct from #939: #939 makes reactivation itself fail only when the email was reused; this issue occurs after a successful reactivation with no email collision.
title: [AuthService][Reactivation][Profiles] Reactivated accounts retain hidden profile tombstones that break later profile writes

## Component

`[AuthService][Roles][Soft Delete][Administration]`

## Severity

P2 High — deleting a custom role permanently tombstones its name, while recreation passes validation and crashes with a unique violation.

## Source evidence

- `CreateRoleCommandHandler.cs:28-39` checks only visible/non-deleted roles; Auth's global query filter also hides deleted roles.
- `DeleteRoleCommandHandler.cs:61-68` soft-deletes an unused custom role.
- `RoleConfiguration.cs:61,64` combines an unconditional unique index on `NormalizedName` with a global `!IsDeleted` query filter.
- The create path does not restore the deleted role or catch/map the database uniqueness race.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. As Admin, create an unused custom role named `Auditor`.
2. Delete that role successfully.
3. Create another role named `Auditor`.
4. The create precheck cannot see the deleted row and reports the name available.
5. PostgreSQL rejects the insert with `23505`; the request returns an uncontrolled 500.

- Admin cannot recreate an accidentally deleted custom role using its business name.
- Automation that reconciles a desired role catalog repeatedly fails.
- A routine admin lifecycle produces a server error instead of an actionable response.

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/AccountConfiguration.cs:157-161` makes email unique only for active rows (`WHERE is_deleted = false`), intentionally releasing an email after soft deletion.

2. A is soft-deleted within the 90-day reactivation window.
3. Account B registers using the now-released `user@example.com`; this is allowed by the partial unique index.
4. Request reactivation for A and submit its valid OTP to reactivate-verify.
5. The handler changes A to `is_deleted=false` and saves.

The application allows the documented preconditions, then relies on the database to throw an unhandled uniqueness exception during restore.

Reactivation must detect that the identity has been reclaimed and return a stable conflict response without attempting a violating update.

- A valid 90-day reactivation flow crashes at its final step.
- Users receive a server error instead of the documented actionable conflict.
- Database exception details may leak through logs/diagnostics, and retrying the same OTP cannot succeed.

- Check for another active account owning the normalized email before restore.
- Return HTTP 409 with a stable error code/message when the email is taken.
- Retain the DB unique index as the final concurrency guard.

## Source evidence

- `services/AuthService/src/AuthService.Infrastructure/Implements/Helpers/JwtHelper.cs:61-75` emits a `kid` header for the configured signing key.
- `JwtHelper.cs:124-150` manually validates against both `JwtSettings:SecretKey` and `JwtSettings:PreviousSecretKey`, with current/previous key IDs.
- `deploy/helm/solar-battery/templates/shared/secret.yaml:48-53` explicitly documents a one-hour previous-key grace period during rotation.

- That shared JwtBearer registration reads only `SecretKey` and configures a singular `IssuerSigningKey`; it never reads `PreviousSecretKey`, `SigningKeyId`, or `PreviousSigningKeyId`.

## Reproduction

1. Configure current key/key ID as v1 and issue a valid access token.
2. Rotate to current v2 while setting `PreviousSecretKey=v1` and `PreviousSigningKeyId=v1`, as documented by the chart.
3. Call `JwtHelper.ValidateToken(oldV1Token)`: it succeeds during the grace period.
4. Send the same token to any `[Authorize]` endpoint in AuthService or another backend service.
5. JwtBearer rejects it with HTTP 401 / `INVALID_SIGNATURE` because only v2 is in `IssuerSigningKey`.

## Actual

Manual token validation and actual HTTP authorization implement different key sets. The configured previous key is ineffective for real API requests.

## Expected

Every token-validation path must resolve `kid` against the same bounded current/previous key ring and honor the documented grace period.

## Impact

- Every active user is forced out during a routine signing-key rotation.
- All services fail simultaneously, creating a platform-wide authentication incident.
- Healthier current-key login/refresh does not protect in-flight clients or requests from mass 401 failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Configure JwtBearer `IssuerSigningKeys` or a safe `IssuerSigningKeyResolver` with current and previous keys/IDs.
- Reject unknown/missing `kid` according to one explicit compatibility policy.
- Keep helper, Gateway, AuthService, and every direct resource-service port semantically identical.
- Remove the previous key after the bounded grace period without restart ambiguity.
- Add integration tests that issue v1, rotate to v2+previous-v1, and prove v1/v2 behavior across Auth, Gateway, Battery, Ticket, Notification, and FileStorage.
- Add negative tests for wrong key, wrong `kid`, expired token, and previous-key removal.

## Verification gap

Existing Shared JWT tests pass 6/6 and JwtHelper tests pass 19/19, but neither suite exercises previous-key JwtBearer authorization.

## Dedupe

Distinct from #925, which covers revocation enforcement. This issue concerns signature validation during an explicitly supported key-rotation grace window.
title: [AuthService][Shared JWT][Key Rotation] Previous signing key is ignored by ASP.NET authentication across all services

## Component

`[IoT][LittleFS][Offline Queue][MQTT TLS]`

## Severity

P2 High — a mount failure silently erases durable telemetry and the provisioned MQTT trust anchor.

## Source evidence

- `firmware-esp32/src/queue/local_queue.cpp:105-108` mounts LittleFS with `LittleFS.begin(true)`, enabling automatic format on mount failure.
- `firmware-esp32/src/net/mqtt_client.cpp:71-74` independently uses the same `LittleFS.begin(true)` behavior while loading the MQTT CA certificate.
- The same filesystem stores `/queue/*.json`, `/queue/*.idem`, and `MQTT_CA_CERT_PATH`.
- `main.cpp` calls `queueBegin()` before `mqttBegin()` during every boot, so the queue path can format the shared partition before MQTT checks whether its CA still exists.

## Reproduction

1. Put one or more offline telemetry batches in `/queue/` and a valid CA at `MQTT_CA_CERT_PATH`.
2. Reboot while fault-injecting a recoverable/transient LittleFS mount failure or filesystem metadata corruption.
3. `queueBegin()` calls `LittleFS.begin(true)`; the library formats the partition and retries the mount.
4. Queue startup reports an empty queue rather than a durability fault.
5. `mqttBegin()` then cannot find the CA certificate and permanently falls back to HTTPS-only until the filesystem image/certificate is reprovisioned.

The same destructive behavior can be triggered from `loadCaCert()` if it is the first effective mount caller in another startup path.

## Actual

The firmware treats a mount problem as permission to format shared persistent storage without confirmation, backup, quarantine, recovery attempt, or a data-loss signal.

## Expected

Production startup must fail safe: preserve the partition, expose the storage fault, and attempt explicit/recoverable repair. Formatting must be a deliberate maintenance/factory-reset operation, never an automatic mount side effect.

## Impact

- All queued telemetry can be lost precisely after an outage or unstable-power event.
- The MQTT CA trust anchor is erased, disabling the primary transport after reboot.
- Operators see queue depth zero and an apparently unrelated missing-CA error, obscuring the destructive root cause.

## Acceptance criteria

- Mount production LittleFS with `formatOnFail=false`.
- Put queue data and immutable/provisioned trust anchors in separately managed partitions or provide an atomic restore path.
- Add explicit, authenticated factory-reset/reformat behavior with clear data-loss warnings.
- Emit durable diagnostics/metrics when mount, recovery, or integrity validation fails.
- Add reboot/fault-injection tests proving transient mount failure and corrupt queue entries do not erase unaffected batches or the CA.
- Verify MQTT and HTTPS fallback behavior after storage recovery.

## Dedupe

Distinct from #883 (enqueue/short-read atomicity), #835 (missing idempotency sidecar), and #892 (certificate-script credential exposure). This issue is destructive automatic formatting of the shared persistence partition during mount.
title: [IoT][LittleFS][Data Loss] Automatic mount recovery erases the offline queue and MQTT CA certificate

## Component

`BatteryService` — IoT device heartbeat configuration and offline detection.

## Summary

Admin APIs accept `HeartbeatIntervalSeconds` up to 3,600 seconds, but offline detection uses one global 300-second threshold and never considers each device's configured interval. A valid low-frequency device is marked Offline, generates an alert/event, and then flips back Active on its next scheduled heartbeat. The API documentation itself warns of the false positive but still permits the incompatible configuration.

## Evidence

- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/CQRS/Command/IotDevice/CreateIotDeviceCommand.cs:50-51` and `UpdateIotDeviceCommand.cs:46-47` accept intervals in `[10, 3600]`.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/Services/IotDeviceOfflineDetectionService.cs:30-42` computes a single `now - offlineAfterSeconds` cutoff for all devices and does not read `HeartbeatIntervalSeconds`.
- `IotDeviceOfflineDetectionService.cs:47-101` marks the device Offline and creates an alert/outbox event.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Infrastructure/BackgroundServices/IotDeviceOfflineDetectionBackgroundService.cs:33` defaults the global threshold to 300 seconds.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Api/Controllers/IotDevicesController.cs:133-138` explicitly documents that setting heartbeat near/above the threshold causes false-positive offline state.
- The next accepted heartbeat flips Offline back to Active at `DeviceLifecycleHandlers.cs:168-173`.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Create/update an IoT device with `HeartbeatIntervalSeconds=3600` (valid input).
2. Keep the device healthy but do not produce sensor batches during the interval (for example a heartbeat-only device or temporary BMS outage).
3. Send one heartbeat, then wait slightly over 300 seconds.
4. Offline worker marks the device Offline and emits `DeviceOffline` alert/event.
5. At the valid one-hour cadence, the next heartbeat changes it back to Active; the cycle repeats.

## Actual result

An allowed heartbeat schedule is incompatible with the system's liveness detector and creates oscillating false incidents.

## Expected result

Offline detection must derive a per-device deadline from its configured heartbeat cadence (with a documented grace/missed-heartbeat count), or validation must reject intervals that cannot satisfy the global threshold.

## Impact

- False offline alerts/notifications and operational noise.
- Device status dashboards oscillate despite a healthy, correctly configured device.
- Real outages become harder to distinguish from configuration-induced false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- Use a per-device cutoff such as `max(global minimum, HeartbeatIntervalSeconds × missed-heartbeat allowance)` or constrain configuration accordingly.
- Define how successful telemetry and MQTT LWT interact with heartbeat liveness.
- Recalculate safely after interval changes.
- Add tests for 10s, 60s, 300s, and 3600s intervals; no device is marked offline before its own deadline.
- Verify exactly one offline event/alert per real transition and clean recovery.

## Dedupe note

Full issue search found no existing per-device heartbeat/offline-threshold issue through #930. Distinct from #870 (MQTT connect partial success), #906 (heartbeat fields dropped), and #922 (firmware discards heartbeat ACK controls).
title: [BatteryService][IoT][Offline Detection] Valid heartbeat intervals exceed the global threshold and create false offline alerts

## Summary

The real firmware instantiates and samples exactly one INA226, then copies that single bus voltage/current pair into a `redundant` reading for every battery serial returned by BMS polling. In the default four-battery setup, three batteries receive measurements from the wrong electrical circuit, which can create false SensorMismatch alerts/tickets or hide a real mismatch.

## Evidence

- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/sensor/ina226.cpp:27` creates one `INA226` at one configured address.
- `ina226.cpp:89-100` samples that device once and explicitly says the same V/I is replicated for every battery.
- `ina226.cpp:101-136` loops through all serials and assigns the identical `v` and `i` to each battery identity with `sensorSourceCode="redundant"`.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/bms/bms_source.cpp:77-84` passes every successfully polled battery serial to that replication method.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/include/config.example.h:165-173` supports only a single INA226 address while the BMS path defaults to four units.
- `../iot/overall.iot.md:88-99` specifies 2–4 independent INA226 modules and per-battery cross-source measurement.
- `overall.md:7949,9685-9688` defines per-battery BMS-versus-INA226 validation, not one aggregate reading cloned across assets.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Configure four battery mappings and connect the single configured INA226 to BAT-1 at 12.8 V / 1 A.
2. Let the other BMS devices report distinct values, e.g. BAT-2=25.6 V, BAT-3=48 V, BAT-4=51.2 V.
3. Call `bmsSourcePollAll` in real mode.
4. Observe four `redundant` records, all carrying 12.8 V / 1 A but labeled as BAT-1 through BAT-4.
5. Backend cross-source comparison treats each as a real measurement of its labeled battery.

## Actual result

One physical measurement is falsified as N independent battery measurements.

## Expected result

Each redundant reading must come from the INA226 physically mapped to that battery. If a battery has no independent sensor, no redundant reading should be emitted for it.

## Impact

- Healthy batteries can generate false voltage/current mismatch alerts and automatic P1/P2 tickets.
- A real failure may be hidden when a cloned value happens to match the wrong BMS.
- Historical telemetry attributes one circuit's measurement to unrelated assets.
- The system reports cross-source redundancy that the hardware/software path does not actually provide.

## Acceptance criteria

- Configure an explicit battery↔INA226 address/channel mapping and instantiate/poll each sensor independently.
- Never clone one physical measurement across multiple battery identities.
- Omit the redundant source for unmapped/unavailable sensors and expose per-sensor health.
- Add real-path tests with distinct per-battery voltages/currents and missing sensors.

## Summary

The real firmware derives the serial list for INA226 and DS18B20 exclusively from successful Modbus BMS readings. If the RS485 bus or all BMS units fail, `nBms=0`, both independent sensor builders receive an empty list, and no telemetry is published even when INA226/DS18B20 are healthy. The implementation therefore removes the very redundancy that is intended to preserve observation when one source fails.

## Evidence

- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/bms/bms_source.cpp:69-75` polls BMS first into `bmsReadings`.
- `bms_source.cpp:77-88` creates `serials[]` only from those successful BMS results and passes `nBms` to both INA226 and DS18B20 builders.
- `bms_source.cpp:90-112` also iterates merge output only while `b < nBms`.
- With `nBms=0`, `bmsSourcePollAll` returns 0; `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:248-255` exits `ingestOnce` without MQTT/HTTPS publication.
- `../iot/docs/glossary.md:74` states the redundancy requirement: BMS + INA226 must ensure one failed source is still detectable.
- `../iot/overall.iot.md:88-99,421-442` defines INA226/DS18B20 as independent cross-source sensors.
- `overall.md:7949,9685-9688` requires three readings per battery and explicitly defines BMS versus INA226 as independent sources.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Run `esp32-s3-real` with healthy INA226 and DS18B20 devices and valid static battery mappings.
2. Disconnect the RS485 bus or make every Modbus slave time out.
3. `modbusReadMultiDrop` returns 0.
4. `ina226BuildRedundantReadings(serials, 0, ...)` and `ds18b20BuildExternalTempReadings(serials, 0, ...)` produce 0 without sampling/publishing mapped batteries.
5. Merge loop runs zero times, `bmsSourcePollAll` returns 0, and the ingest path publishes nothing.

Failure of the primary BMS source suppresses all independent redundant/external sensor data.

## Expected result

Every configured battery mapping must be sampled independently by each available sensor source. A BMS failure should omit only the primary reading and preserve INA226/DS18B20 readings with correct battery identity.

## Impact

- Primary BMS failure creates a complete telemetry blackout instead of degraded but observable operation.
- Cross-source monitoring cannot distinguish BMS failure from gateway outage.
- Independent voltage/current/temperature safety data is lost exactly when redundancy is needed.
- Downstream offline/anomaly/ticket behavior receives no evidence of the partial hardware failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- Build the battery serial/mapping list from provisioned/static battery mappings, not successful BMS results.
- Poll and merge BMS, INA226, and DS18B20 independently; preserve source tags and identity.
- Emit partial batches when one or two sources fail.
- Expose per-source health/failure telemetry.
- Add real-path tests for BMS-only failure, INA-only failure, DS-only failure, mixed per-battery failure, and all sources failed.
- Assert a healthy redundant source remains published when `nBms=0`.

## Component

`BatteryService` ↔ `IoT firmware` — heartbeat acknowledgement/control contract.

## Summary

BatteryService returns `NextHeartbeatInSeconds`, `ClockSkewWarning`, server time, and `FirmwareUpdateAvailable` on every heartbeat, and its API contract explicitly tells firmware to apply these controls. ESP32 sends heartbeat through a response-discarding helper and never parses the acknowledgement. Runtime interval changes are ignored, clock-drift recovery is not triggered, and OTA hints cannot accelerate a required update.

## Evidence

- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/CQRS/Handler/IotDevice/DeviceLifecycleHandlers.cs:185-196` returns the four control fields from live device state.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Api/Controllers/IotDevicesController.cs:130-138` documents that the device should use `NextHeartbeatInSeconds`, auto-resync on clock warning, and act on firmware-update hints.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/telemetry/heartbeat.cpp:96-121` calls `httpPostJson`, checks only the status code, and never parses a body.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/net/http_client.cpp:243-247` invokes the internal client with a null response buffer.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/telemetry/heartbeat.cpp:125-159` changes cadence only through `heartbeatBegin`/`heartbeatSetInterval`; no ACK path calls the setter.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/provision/provision.cpp:138-151` persists the interval only during provisioning.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:94-120` marks provisioning done and does not refresh the config on later heartbeats.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Provision a device with `HeartbeatIntervalSeconds=60`; firmware stores/uses 60 seconds.
2. Change the device interval through the admin API to 10 seconds.
3. Let the device send its next heartbeat. BatteryService returns HTTP 200 with `data.nextHeartbeatInSeconds=10`.
4. Firmware discards the body and keeps `s_intervalMs=60000`; later heartbeats remain 60 seconds apart.
5. The same trace shows `clockSkewWarning=true` or `firmwareUpdateAvailable=true` is also ignored.

## Actual result

HTTP success is counted, but none of the server's heartbeat controls affect device behavior.

## Expected result

Firmware must validate and apply the acknowledgement atomically, with bounded values and explicit fallback when the body is invalid.

## Impact

- Admin heartbeat-cadence changes do not take effect without reprovision/reset, causing stale offline detection or excess load.
- Clock-drift warnings cannot request immediate resynchronization.
- Required firmware updates may wait for the separate hourly poll instead of acting on the server hint.
- Backend exposes a control-plane contract that the shipped device cannot consume.

## Acceptance criteria

- Receive and parse the full `CommonResponse<IotHeartbeatAckDto>` body.
- Validate/apply `NextHeartbeatInSeconds` within [10, 3600] and persist the chosen cadence when required.
- Trigger immediate NTP resync on `ClockSkewWarning` and schedule an immediate bounded firmware check on `FirmwareUpdateAvailable`.
- Preserve the current cadence and emit a diagnostic metric/log on malformed ACK.
- Add cross-repository tests for live interval change, clock warning, firmware hint, malformed body, and retry/idempotency behavior.

## Dedupe note

Full issue search found no existing heartbeat-ACK/NextHeartbeat/ClockSkewWarning defect through #921. Distinct from #858 (MQTT polling interval persistence), #859 (unsupported MQTT command type), and #906 (heartbeat request fields accepted but not persisted).
title: [IoT][BatteryService][Heartbeat ACK] Firmware discards server cadence, clock-skew, and OTA controls

## Component

`IoT firmware` — real BMS Modbus multi-drop polling and main-loop availability.

## Summary

Firmware documents/configures a 500 ms Modbus timeout through `BMS_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS`, but never applies it. The pinned ModbusMaster library uses a hard-coded 2,000 ms response timeout. With one retry and four configured BMS unit IDs, an offline RS485 bus blocks the single Arduino loop for about 16 seconds per poll, delaying safety sensors, heartbeat, OTA verification, queue flush, and MQTT servicing.

## Evidence

- `../iot/firmware-esp32/include/config.example.h:158-163` configures 4 unit IDs, `BMS_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS=500`, and one retry.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/bms/modbus_bms.cpp:102-131` performs each request plus retry but never references the timeout setting.
- `modbus_bms.cpp:209-228` polls every configured unit synchronously in sequence.
- Pinned `ModbusMaster/src/ModbusMaster.h:251-252` hard-codes `ku16MBResponseTimeout=2000` ms, and `ModbusMaster.cpp:800-803` waits for it inside the transaction loop.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:241-255,530-539` calls the synchronous BMS poll from `ingestOnce()`.
- `main.cpp:542-567` cannot run queue flush, OTA, heartbeat, SHT31, MQ-2, water-leak, LED, or stats until that call returns.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Build/run the `esp32-s3-real` profile with the documented defaults: 4 BMS unit IDs, one retry, configured timeout 500 ms.
2. Disconnect or power off every Modbus slave while ESP32 itself remains online.
3. Each unit performs two transactions at the library's 2,000 ms hard-coded timeout.
4. Total blocking time is approximately `4 units × 2 attempts × 2,000 ms = 16,000 ms`, plus settle delays.
5. Observe that the following main-loop ticks do not execute during the block, despite a 5-second ingest interval and shorter safety-sensor poll intervals.

## Actual result

The advertised 500 ms timeout has no effect. Failure of the BMS bus stalls unrelated networking, OTA, heartbeat, and environmental safety work in the single-threaded loop.

## Expected result

One failed peripheral bus must not block unrelated safety/network tasks beyond the configured timeout; the effective timeout must match configuration and the poller must have a bounded total budget.

## Impact

- Gas/water incident detection and reporting can be delayed by roughly 16 seconds per failed poll.
- Heartbeat, OTA health/rollback checks, MQTT polling, and queued telemetry are starved.
- The provisioned 5-second telemetry cadence cannot be met under a common partial-hardware failure.
- Adding more unit IDs linearly increases the stall.

## Acceptance criteria

- Apply an actually supported per-request timeout or replace/wrap the library with a configurable transaction deadline.
- Enforce a bounded total multi-drop poll budget and yield/state-machine behavior so unrelated ticks continue.
- Report individual BMS timeout health without blocking other units/sensors.
- Add a real-target/fake-clock test for all slaves offline and one slave offline.
- Assert maximum loop latency and that OTA/heartbeat/MQ-2/water ticks still run within their deadlines.
- Remove or fail build on unused timeout configuration.

## Dedupe note

Full repository issue search found no existing BMS/Modbus timeout or loop-starvation issue through #920. This is distinct from #869 (INA226 I²C failure), #882 (DS18B20 probe fan-out), #884 (real profile shipping mock), and #904 (JK-BMS current decoding).
title: [IoT][BMS][Availability] Unused 500 ms timeout lets offline multi-drop polling block the main loop for about 16 seconds

## Component

`BatteryService` ↔ `IoT firmware` — OTA firmware-check response contract.

## Summary

BatteryService accepts and stores unbounded firmware `ReleaseNotes`, while ESP32 firmware copies the complete firmware-check response into a fixed 2,048-byte buffer. Any valid release whose JSON exceeds 2,047 bytes is silently truncated; JSON parsing then fails and the device never downloads or applies the update.

## Evidence

- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/CQRS/Command/IotFirmware/CreateIotFirmwareReleaseCommand.cs:23-24,36-51` accepts `ReleaseNotes` but imposes no size limit.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/IotFirmwareReleaseConfiguration.cs:40-41` maps `release_notes` with no maximum length.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/DTOs/IotDeviceDto.cs:123-160` returns both alias pairs (`UpdateAvailable`/`HasUpdate`, `ArtifactUrl`/`DownloadUrl`) plus the full `ReleaseNotes`, increasing the response size.
- `services/BatteryService/src/BatteryService.Application/CQRS/Handler/IotDevice/DeviceLifecycleHandlers.cs:205-255` creates a Pending update log and returns the full notes.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/ota/ota_update.cpp:298-310` allocates exactly `char resp[2048]` and aborts when truncated JSON cannot be parsed.
- `../iot/firmware-esp32/src/net/http_client.cpp:36-51` copies only `fullBufLen - 1` bytes and returns the truncated length without exposing a truncation error.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Create and publish a valid firmware release with a `ReleaseNotes` string of 2,500 ASCII characters; the backend validator and database accept it.
2. Assign it as the target of a device and call `GET /api/iot-devices/firmware-check?currentVersion=<old>`.
3. The JSON response necessarily exceeds the firmware's 2,047-byte payload capacity.
4. `copyResponseFull` truncates the body and null-terminates it; `deserializeJson` returns an error.
5. The device logs `firmware-check JSON parse FAIL (response truncated?)` and never reaches `downloadAndFlash`.
6. On a later poll, BatteryService creates another Pending update log because the target remains different.

## Actual result

A release accepted by BatteryService cannot be consumed by the shipped firmware. The update is silently skipped after HTTP 200, while Pending attempt logs can accumulate.

## Expected result

Every response permitted by the backend contract must fit the device protocol, or the firmware must stream/parse safely and explicitly reject over-limit payloads before creating an update attempt.

## Impact

- Required safety/security firmware can be blocked by ordinary release notes.
- Operators see Pending attempts but devices never report Downloading/Failed.
- Repeated polls create misleading orphan Pending logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define and enforce a shared maximum response/release-notes size, or omit release notes from the device check payload.
- Do not serialize duplicate alias fields on the wire.
- Firmware must detect `Content-Length`/buffer overflow and report a terminal, diagnosable failure rather than parse a truncated body.
- Do not create repeated Pending logs for responses the device cannot consume.
- Add a cross-repository contract test at the maximum permitted notes/URL lengths and an over-limit negative test.

## Dedupe note

Checked against E2E issues #722–#914, including #905, #912 and #913. Those cover version registration and artifact storage/upload; none covers firmware-check response truncation.
title: [BatteryService][IoT][OTA Contract] Valid release notes truncate firmware-check JSON and block updates

## Component

`[IoT][HTTPS Fallback][Backoff]` — firmware ingest admission during BatteryService/network failure and fleet retry jitter.

## Source evidence

- `firmware-esp32/src/main.cpp:304-313` calls `s_backoff.recordFailure()` after a transient POST and logs the delay.
- `tryFlushQueue()` at `main.cpp:318-365` respects `s_backoff.nextRetryAt()`, but the normal ingest scheduler at `main.cpp:524-543` never checks it before calling `ingestOnce()` and `postBatch()`.
- Therefore every newly sampled batch performs another HTTP request at `pollInterval` even while the logged backoff window is active; only old queue flushing is delayed.
- `net/backoff.cpp:25-31` initializes one process-global jitter RNG with constant `0x12345678`.
- `Backoff::setRandomSeed()` is used by tests only and is never called at firmware startup, despite `backoff.h` claiming a runtime/default seed. Every device follows the same jitter sequence.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Configure fallback HTTPS with a 5-second poll and make BatteryService return 503 or 429 continuously.
2. Observe the first failures increase/log backoff (eventually tens of seconds to five minutes).
3. Capture requests during a period where `millis() < nextRetryAt()`.
4. Observe a new POST every five seconds from the normal ingest path; only `tryFlushQueue()` is suppressed.
5. Start two devices from the same firmware and compare their delay sequence; both generate the same jitter values because the seed is constant.

## Actual result

The firmware advertises exponential backoff but continues sending fixed-rate live requests through the entire backoff window. A fleet retries in a synchronized deterministic pattern, and repeated live failures keep moving the shared queue-flush deadline.

## Expected result

An active retry/admission window applies to all HTTP attempts for the failed dependency. New samples are durably queued without another request until the deadline. Devices use independent entropy and honor server retry guidance.

## Impact

A BatteryService outage or 429 overload is amplified by every gateway (for a 5-second poll, up to 12 requests/minute/device), delaying recovery and defeating the intended thundering-herd protection. Oldest queued data is also starved behind ongoing live failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Gate live fallback POST and queue flush through one overflow-safe retry/admission controller.
- While backoff is active, enqueue new telemetry directly without attempting HTTP.
- Seed jitter from per-device/boot entropy (for example `esp_random` plus device identity), not a fleet-wide constant.
- Parse/honor bounded `Retry-After` for 429/503 where available.
- Ensure successful recovery drains oldest-first without new data starving queued records.
- Add native/simulator tests for active-window suppression, increasing/capped delay, two-device jitter divergence, 429/503, millis wrap, and recovery ordering.
- Add request/queue/backoff metrics that distinguish live attempts from flush attempts.

## Dedupe note

Distinct from #741 (environmental incident permanent-4xx tight retry) and #883/#835 (LittleFS queue atomicity). This issue is the main telemetry HTTPS admission/backoff path under transient failure.
title: [IoT][HTTPS Fallback][Backoff] Live batches bypass backoff and every device uses identical jitter

## Component

`[BatteryService][OTA Upload][Storage]` — validation, atomicity, and cleanup of uploaded firmware binaries.

## Source evidence

- `AdminIotFirmwareReleasesController.cs:273-294` checks only non-empty file and `.bin` extension.
- Endpoint request cap is 60 MiB (`:259-261`), but no `File.Length <= 50 MB`, Version, or HardwareRevision validation runs before `File.Create` at `:302-325`.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Upload a 55 MB file named `.bin` with empty Version and HardwareRevision.
2. Observe upload 201 and a full file under the firmware storage root.
3. Attempt release creation with the returned metadata; observe validation 400.
4. Repeat; the default 2 GiB PVC can be exhausted with a few dozen authorized requests. Also cancel a streaming upload and inspect the partial file.

## Actual result

Artifacts that can never become valid releases are permanently written under final names. Failures/cancellation and abandoned two-step workflows have no cleanup.

## Expected result

All metadata/size constraints are validated before allocation, writes are temporary/atomic, and uncommitted artifacts have explicit lifecycle cleanup.

## Impact

An authorized admin mistake or repeated request fills persistent storage, leaves misleading binaries, and can take File/OTA functions offline. Partial files may be mistaken for complete artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Validate required metadata, enum/length constraints, and the same 50 MB byte limit before creating a file.
- Stream to a `.part`/temporary object, verify actual length/SHA, and atomically commit the final name.
- Delete temporary/partial data on cancellation or any exception.
- Link uploads to release metadata through a transaction/state machine or expire unattached artifacts safely.
- Add tests proving rejected/oversized/cancelled/failed-create flows do not increase durable file count/usage.
- Add quota/metrics/alerts for firmware storage consumption.

## Component

`[BatteryService][OTA Storage Contract]` — artifact persistence and URL generation in both documented production storage modes.

- Compose/Helm defaults leave `Firmware__PublicBaseUrl` empty.
- `AdminIotFirmwareReleasesController.cs:328-332` then returns a relative artifact URL `/firmware-storage/{file}` after upload.

- `Program.cs:138-149` and the controller at `:296-332` still write only to a local fallback directory and concatenate the CDN base with the filename.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Default mode: upload a valid small `.bin`, receive 201 with a relative URL, then POST create-release using the returned data. Observe validation 400 for non-absolute `ArtifactUrl`.
2. Object mode: follow the documented no-PVC/CDN configuration and upload a valid binary. Request the returned CDN URL and restart the pod. Observe the object does not exist externally and local data is ephemeral.

## Actual result

Neither documented storage mode produces a durable URL that can complete upload → create release → device download.

## Expected result

One storage abstraction persists the artifact first and returns an externally reachable durable absolute URL whose semantics are accepted by release creation.

## Impact

OTA rollout cannot be completed in default production and can register broken URLs in object mode. Devices receive unusable download locations and uploaded files become orphaned/lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- Implement a storage abstraction with real local/PVC and S3-compatible/object-storage adapters.
- Local mode returns an absolute externally reachable URL (or release creation deliberately resolves trusted relative paths consistently).
- Object mode uploads successfully before returning a CDN/object URL; rollback the object on failed metadata commit.

## Component

`[Shared][Pagination][Overflow]` — calculation of database offsets in Audit, Auth, Battery, Notification, and Ticket list handlers.

## Source evidence

- `shared/src/SharedContracts/Common/Requests/PaginationRequest.cs:9-18` normalizes non-positive values and caps `PageSize`, but has no maximum `PageNumber` or offset bound.
- At least 33 handlers calculate `Skip((PageNumber - 1) * PageSize)` using unchecked 32-bit integers.
- With `PageNumber=2147483647` and `PageSize=100`, the multiplication wraps to `-200`; EF/Npgsql translates that into an invalid negative OFFSET or otherwise fails the request.

## Steps to reproduce

Call a PostgreSQL-backed list endpoint using the shared request, for example an authorized Battery/Auth/Audit list route, with:

```text
?pageNumber=2147483647&pageSize=100
```

Inspect the generated offset and HTTP response.

## Actual result

The accepted positive page number overflows the offset calculation and can produce a 5xx/database error rather than an empty page or controlled validation response.

## Expected result

The API rejects an unrepresentable page/offset with 400/422, or calculates a safe checked 64-bit offset within a documented maximum.

## Impact

Any caller can induce repeatable exceptions across many list endpoints and pollute logs/availability using one query value.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a shared maximum page/offset or calculate with checked `long` and validate provider limits.
- Return a consistent 400/422 ProblemDetails/CommonResponse for overflow/out-of-range input.
- Replace duplicated unchecked expressions with one safe pagination helper.
- Add shared boundary tests and at least one real PostgreSQL endpoint test for `int.MaxValue`, max valid, and max+1.
- Inventory all handlers so no alternate pagination DTO retains the same overflow.

## Dedupe note

Distinct from #797, which covers negative and unbounded pagination in specific Ticket chat/saga routes; this is positive integer overflow in the shared request across services.
title: [Shared][Pagination][Overflow] Extreme PageNumber wraps database offsets and causes 5xx

- `iot/firmware-esp32/platformio.ini:59-65` hard-codes the production/main firmware `FW_VERSION` as `0.1.0-sprint4`; `esp32-s3-real` inherits it at `:116-121`.
- `BatteryService.Application/.../CreateIotFirmwareReleaseCommand.cs:39-42` accepts only `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`, so `0.1.0-sprint4` cannot be registered as a release target.
- Firmware check sends that build constant as `currentVersion` and compares strings exactly (`ota_update.cpp:292-320`).
- Before flashing, it persists the backend target string at `ota_update.cpp:341-350`.
- After reboot, `ota_update.cpp:369-378` requires `strcmp(FW_VERSION, targetVersion) == 0`; any mismatch is recorded as Failed and the target is marked bad.
- `config.example.h:229-232` explicitly documents that exact equality is mandatory, but the shipped build flag violates the backend's accepted format.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Build either main firmware environment without editing source. Its embedded version is `0.1.0-sprint4`.
2. Attempt to create a BatteryService firmware release with version `0.1.0-sprint4`; validation rejects it because the only accepted form is `X.Y.Z`.
3. Register the closest valid target `0.1.0` and upload the unchanged artifact.
4. Let a device check, download, verify SHA, flash, and reboot.
5. `handleVerify()` compares running `0.1.0-sprint4` with target `0.1.0`, reports `boot version mismatch`, clears verification, and marks `0.1.0` bad even though the intended binary booted.

## Actual result

No release record can have the exact version embedded in the shipped firmware. Using a backend-valid version makes post-flash verification fail deterministically and blocks/poisons subsequent delivery of that target.

## Expected result

The build pipeline and backend share one validated version value. The version stored in release metadata, embedded in the binary, returned by firmware-check, and observed after reboot is byte-for-byte identical.

## Impact

The completed OTA feature cannot reach Success with artifacts built from the checked-in production environments. Operators can misdiagnose a healthy image as failed/bad, lose rollout capability, and remain on vulnerable or faulty firmware.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define one release version input accepted by both build and backend; either support validated SemVer pre-release identifiers end-to-end or embed strict `X.Y.Z`.
- Inject the release version in CI rather than leaving a stale sprint literal in `platformio.ini`.
- Extract/attest the embedded version from the produced artifact and reject upload/registration when it differs from release metadata.
- Add an E2E fixture covering create release → firmware-check → flash/reboot simulation → Success with exact version equality.
- Add a negative test proving a mismatched artifact is rejected before rollout, not discovered only after flashing.
- Ensure bad-version state is not written for a metadata mismatch caused by the release pipeline itself.

## Component

`[IoT][BMS][JK-BMS][Safety]` — Modbus register decoding for the documented JK-BD6A24S10P/JK-BMS path.

## Source evidence

- `firmware-esp32/src/bms/bms_register_map.h:105-117` declares JK current at offset 2 as signed **int32**, scaled by `0.001 A`, and explicitly notes that only the low 16 bits are read.
- `firmware-esp32/src/bms/bms_register_map.cpp:37-45` always loads one `uint16_t`, casts it to `int16_t`, and applies the scale; the register-map type has no width/word-order metadata.
- `firmware-esp32/src/bms/modbus_bms.cpp:140-165` receives the full register array but sends it through that 16-bit decoder.
- The hardware assembly guide targets a JK-BD6A24S10P rated for 100 A continuous, so normal operating values exceed the signed-16-bit range at 0.001 A resolution (±32.767 A).
- Existing native tests cover JBD 16-bit positive/negative current only; there is no JK 32-bit boundary test.

## Deterministic reproduction

Encode two valid signed 32-bit JK values using the declared 0.001 A scale:

1. `+50.000 A` → raw `0x0000C350`. The current decoder uses low word `0xC350` as `int16_t -15536` and returns `-15.536 A`.
2. `-50.000 A` → raw `0xFFFF3CB0`. It uses low word `0x3CB0` as `int16_t 15536` and returns `+15.536 A`.

The sign and magnitude both become wrong above 32.767 A even though the Modbus read succeeded.

## Actual result

High charge current can be published as a smaller discharge current, and high discharge current as a smaller charge current. The payload is syntactically valid, so BatteryService persists and evaluates it rather than rejecting it as a sensor fault.

## Expected result

The JK decoder combines both registers with the model's documented word order, performs signed 32-bit conversion, applies the correct scale, and rejects impossible/out-of-range values instead of silently publishing them.

## Impact

Charging-state inference, power/energy calculations, anomaly detection, redundant-sensor comparison, maintenance decisions, and safety alerts can all be inverted during ordinary high-current operation on the documented 100 A rig.

## Acceptance criteria

- Extend register metadata/decoder support for 16-bit and 32-bit signed/unsigned fields plus explicit word order.
- Decode JK current from both registers according to the exact supported JK protocol/hardware revision.
- Add sanity limits and surface an invalid sensor read rather than a believable incorrect value.
- Add native vectors for `0`, `±32.767 A`, `±32.768 A`, `±50 A`, and documented extrema in both word orders.
- Add a hardware/recorded-frame comparison against the JK app or a protocol fixture and verify voltage/current/SOC across the whole supported range.
- Ensure downstream telemetry/alerts are not emitted from a failed decode.
title: [IoT][BMS][JK-BMS][Safety] Signed 32-bit current is truncated to 16 bits and reverses charge direction

```bash
  | head -1; then
  echo "::error::Private key hoặc passwd file đã từng commit vào git history!"
  exit 1

```

Without `set -o pipefail`, an empty pipeline still has the exit status of `head`, which is zero. Therefore the `if` body is taken even when `grep` found no secret file.

## Deterministic reproduction

Run the exact pipeline in the IoT repository where the secret filename query returns no line. The pipeline status is still `0`, and the condition enters the failure branch.

The security guard reports a committed private key/passwd on a clean history result and makes `Infra config sanity` red unconditionally. A permanently red check cannot distinguish a real secret incident from the false positive and is likely to be ignored or bypassed.

## Expected result

The step fails only when a matching secret filename exists and succeeds otherwise, while preserving the match as audit evidence without printing secret contents.

The repository has no trustworthy green CI baseline for MQTT infrastructure. Real secret regressions are hidden in constant noise, merge protection can be disabled/bypassed, and unrelated changes are blocked.

- Base the condition on `grep -q` (or enable `pipefail` and handle SIGPIPE correctly) instead of the final `head` status.
- Suppress secret contents; report only a safe path/count.
- Add a fixture/test proving no-match succeeds and a synthetic matched filename fails.
- Re-run the workflow and obtain a green `Infra config sanity` job on clean history.
- Keep an explicit incident/rotation path when a real historical secret is found.

## Component
IoT firmware — OTA safety / NVS persistence

## Source evidence
- `firmware-esp32/src/ota/ota_update.cpp:344-350` writes `otaLogId`, `otaToVer`, `otaFromVer`, `otaBootN`, and `otaPend` before flashing, but ignores every boolean return value.
- `firmware-esp32/src/config/nvs_store.cpp:66-100` explicitly returns `false` when NVS open/write fails.
- `firmware-esp32/src/ota/ota_update.cpp:354-366` continues download, switches the boot partition, and restarts even if the durable verify/rollback state was not stored.
- On the next boot, `otaBegin()` enters verify mode only when `otaPend == 1` (`ota_update.cpp:434-454`). A failed `otaPend` write therefore bypasses health verification and application rollback entirely.

## Reproduction
1. Enable OTA and return a valid update artifact/checksum/logId.
2. Fault-inject an NVS full/corrupt/open failure before the writes at lines 346-350.
3. Observe `nvsPut*` return false while `downloadAndFlash()` still runs and the device restarts into the new partition.
4. Reboot the new firmware and observe `otaPend` missing, so it is treated as a normal boot and is never health-checked or rolled back.

## Actual
The safety metadata is best-effort. Flashing can proceed without a durable record of the prior/target version, boot counter, pending verification, or rollback report.

## Expected
OTA must abort before writing/switching partitions unless all rollback metadata is durably committed and read back successfully. State should be versioned/checksummed or atomically staged, and all subsequent clear/report writes must handle persistence failure explicitly.

## Impact
A transient NVS failure can turn a recoverable bad OTA into an unrecoverable device deployment, silently bypassing the advertised rollback protection.

## Acceptance criteria
- Check every NVS result and verify the committed state before flashing.
- Do not call `Update.end(true)` or restart when rollback state is unavailable.
- Add fault-injection tests for failure of each OTA state write, partial state, full NVS, and reboot recovery.
- Emit a diagnostic/status failure that is observable by operators.

`SohPredictionBackgroundService` chỉ raise alert khi `Classification ∈ {Degrading, Failed}` (`:165-166`), trong khi AI có thể trả `Normal` kèm `risk.priority = P1` và `warnings[TEMP_CRITICAL]`. Sự cố nhiệt/anomaly nghiêm trọng do đó **không sinh alert, không sinh ticket**.

## Nguyên nhân gốc (đã xác minh trên source)

| # | Nơi | Vấn đề |
|---|-----|--------|
| 1 | `SohPredictionBackgroundService.cs:165-166` | Điều kiện raise chỉ xét `Classification`, bỏ qua `result.Priority` |
| 2 | `AiPredictionResult.cs:74` | `Priority` **đã** được parse (gRPC `:58`, HTTP `:62`) nhưng không nơi nào đọc |

## Scope

**Trong scope:**
- Điều kiện raise alert xét `Priority ∈ {P1, P2}` song song với `Classification`
- Severity = mức cao hơn giữa (classification) và (priority): `Critical > Warning`

- Không đổi luồng Prescribe ngoài việc đổi gate từ `Classification == Failed` sang `severity == Critical`

## Endpoints

Không thêm endpoint. `GET /api/alerts` trả thêm field `aiEvidence` (nullable, backward-compatible).

## Approach

### 1. Severity resolution — lấy mức cao hơn, một nhánh raise duy nhất

Gộp hai nguồn tín hiệu trước khi quyết định. Đúng một nhánh raise → thoả AC "không duplicate với classification branch" theo **cấu trúc**, không phải bằng thêm `if` kiểm tra trùng.

| Classification | Priority | Severity | Ghi chú |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal | None / P3 | *(không alert)* | Hành vi cũ |
| Normal | P2 | Warning | **Mới** — AC #1 |
| Normal | P1 | Critical | **Mới** — repro của issue |
| Degrading | None / P3 | Warning | Hành vi cũ |
| Degrading | P1 | Critical | Nâng theo risk |
| Failed | bất kỳ | Critical | Không bị P2/P3 hạ xuống |

### 2. AnomalyType suy từ warning code

```
TEMP_CRITICAL / TEMP_HIGH  -> Overheat        (SingleAsset, High)
TEMP_LOW                   -> Undertemp
VOLTAGE_HIGH               -> Overvoltage
VOLTAGE_LOW                -> Undervoltage    (NoPower)
SOH_LOW                    -> SohDegradation
(khac)                     -> SohDegradation  (fallback)
```

Lấy warning `severity="critical"` đầu tiên, không có thì phần tử đầu. Hệ quả: `Overheat → (SingleAsset, High)` + category `Overheat`, thay vì `(SingleAsset, Low)` + `Performance`.

### 3. ThresholdValue / ActualValue / Unit theo loại alert

Hiện hardcode `80m / SohPercent / "%"` (`:287-289`) — đúng cho SOH, sai cho alert nhiệt.
`SohDegradation` → giữ nguyên; type khác → cả ba `null` (đều nullable), chi tiết ở `AiEvidence`.

### 4. AiEvidence

JSON `{ risk_level, priority, action_code, warnings[] }`. Chỉ ghi khi thực sự có tín hiệu (tránh cột toàn `{}`). Cột `text` nullable — `warnings[]` không giới hạn số lượng.

### 5. Dedup theo AnomalyType đã tính

`RaiseSohAlertAsync` hardcode `a.AnomalyType == SohDegradation` (`:274`). Khi type biến thiên phải dedup theo **chính type sắp tạo** — nếu không, alert `Overheat` do AI sinh sẽ bị alert `SohDegradation` đang mở nuốt mất.

### 6. Gate Prescribe

Đổi `Classification == Failed` (`:173`) → `severity == Critical`. Nhất quán với quy ước "chỉ Critical mới tạo ticket" (`:297`).

## Steps

- [ ] Bước 1 — Nhánh `fix/GH-805-ai-risk-priority-alert` từ `dev` (tree sạch, 0 ahead/behind)
- [ ] Bước 2 — Entity + Migration `AddAlertAiEvidence`, test rollback theo `be.md §14`, UTF-8 no BOM
- [ ] Bước 3 — Contract: `AiWarningItem.cs` + mở rộng `AiPredictionResult` + 2 static helper `ResolveSeverity`, `MapWarningToAnomalyType`
- [ ] Bước 4 — Parse `warnings[]` / `risk_level` / `action_code` ở cả HTTP và gRPC client
- [ ] Bước 5 — Test trước (đỏ): bảng chân trị severity, map warning code, 4 kịch bản integration
- [ ] Bước 6 — Fix job: `ResolveSeverity` + `anomalyType` + dedup theo type + `AiEvidence` + gate Prescribe
- [ ] Bước 7 — DTO: `AlertDto` + `BatteryMapper.ToDto` (`:108`)
- [ ] Bước 8 — Clean rebuild → `dotnet test` PASS
- [ ] Bước 9 — `/kltn-reviewcode` → `/kltn-test 805` → `/kltn-ship 805`

## Edge Cases

| Case | Hành vi mong đợi |
|------|-----------------|
| `Normal` + `None`/`P3`/rỗng | Không alert (hành vi cũ) |
| `Priority` chuỗi lạ (`"p1"`, `" P1 "`, `"HIGH"`) | `Trim().ToUpperInvariant()` xử lý `p1` / ` P1 `; `HIGH` không match → không raise theo risk |
| `Normal` + `P1`, `warnings` rỗng | Vẫn raise Critical, type fallback `SohDegradation`, `AiEvidence` chỉ có risk block |
| `Failed` + `P2` | Critical — không bị hạ |
| `Failed` + `warnings=[TEMP_CRITICAL]` | Type = `Overheat` — warning critical mô tả sự cố cấp bách hơn |
| Nhiều warning critical | Lấy phần tử đầu — deterministic |
| Warning code chưa biết | Fallback `SohDegradation`, không mất alert |
| Có alert `SohDegradation` mở + prediction ra `Overheat` | Tạo alert mới (khác type) — hai sự cố khác nhau |
| `AiEvidence` khi không risk lẫn warning | `null`, không ghi `"{}"` |
| Response cũ thiếu `warnings`/`risk_level` | List rỗng / `null` → lùi về đúng hành vi hiện tại |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Normal` + `P1` → alert `Critical` + Outbox V1/V2 → sinh ticket
- [ ] `Normal` + `P2` → alert `Warning`, **không** Outbox (giữ quy ước chỉ Critical tạo ticket)
- [ ] `Normal` + `P3`/`None` → **không** tạo alert
- [ ] `Failed` + `P1` → đúng **1** alert, **1** cặp Outbox (không duplicate với nhánh classification)
- [ ] `Degrading` + `P1` → severity `Critical`
- [ ] `Failed` + `P2` → severity vẫn `Critical`
- [ ] Repro của issue (`SOH 95 · score 0 · temp 50°C · TEMP_CRITICAL · P1`) → alert `Overheat` `Critical`, **không** phải `SohDegradation`
- [ ] `Alert.AiEvidence` chứa `risk_level`, `priority`, `action_code`, `warnings[]`
- [ ] HTTP client và gRPC client parity về `Warnings` / `RiskLevel` / `ActionCode`
- [ ] Migration rollback được: `database update <prev>` → `database update` không lỗi
- [ ] Clean rebuild → `dotnet test` BatteryService PASS, coverage ≥ 80%
